bugs.error_message: Formspark POST returns HTTP 500 'Internal server error' on real brief/hello submissions (form RBavvWpyd)
bugs.file: Formspark dashboard (external) — not a code defect
bugs.root_cause: Formspark rejects EVERY submission to form RBavvWpyd as spam: the 500 response carries header `formspark-status: spam`. Reproduced with curl for a minimal token-less JSON body {email,message}, and unchanged by adding form/_gotcha/an invalid g-recaptcha-response, by form-urlencoded body, or by matching Origin/Referer (prod, www, localhost). Because the real site (which sends a valid token) also 500s, the reCAPTCHA verification is failing server-side — the reCAPTCHA SECRET configured in Formspark is missing or does not match the site key (VITE_CAPTCHA_SITEKEY) that mints the token, and/or reCAPTCHA is enabled with the wrong key type (v2-invisible vs v3). Our payload shape is correct (probe 1, simpler than what submit.ts sends, already fails).
bugs.fix: No code change. Dashboard-side: in Formspark form RBavvWpyd's spam/reCAPTCHA settings, set the reCAPTCHA SECRET that pairs with VITE_CAPTCHA_SITEKEY (both must be the same reCAPTCHA v2 'Invisible' key pair), and ensure the reCAPTCHA admin console lists creativecodelogic.com + localhost. If the intent was to launch without captcha, disable reCAPTCHA on the form — then token-less submits succeed. Note: requests sent WITHOUT `Accept: application/json` get a 302 redirect instead of the JSON 500, but that is Formspark's redirect flow, not proof of acceptance.

bugs.error_message: Contact drawer: Send button never enables after solving the reCAPTCHA checkbox (stays disabled/shadowed)
bugs.root_cause: The reCAPTCHA solve happens inside Google's cross-origin iframe and triggers no React re-render, so the submit gate never re-evaluated. (The gate needs a state update driven by the widget's own callback.)
bugs.fix: captcha.ts renderCheckbox now pushes the token to React via an onToken(token) arg wired to the widget's callback/expired-callback/error-callback; HelloDrawer holds captchaToken in state and gates Send on captchaToken !== "" (sends it as g-recaptcha-response, resets to "" after submit + on close). Added a defensive path: renderCheckbox rejection → quiet error state instead of a dead button. Guarded the render with a renderedRef so React StrictMode's double-invoke doesn't throw 'already rendered' and trip that error path.

bugs.error_message: Nav loses its backdrop-blur / .nav-scrolled treatment after the contact drawer closes, until the next scroll
bugs.root_cause: Diagnosed: after close the header STILL carried .nav-scrolled and computed backdrop-filter was still blur(12px) — the class was present, so this is the Chromium compositing bug where unmounting an overlapping backdrop-filter layer (the drawer backdrop's backdrop-blur-sm) drops the nav's backdrop-filter rendering until a repaint. (A separate class-drop on programmatic scroll was proven a test-harness artifact: it reproduces with scrollBy/wheel WITHOUT ever opening the drawer, from scrollIntoView desyncing Lenis vs ScrollTrigger.)
bugs.fix: Removed backdrop-blur-sm from the drawer backdrop; use bg-navy/75 (visually equivalent over the dark contact section) so there is no second backdrop-filter layer to unmount. Also added requestAnimationFrame(() => ScrollTrigger.update()) after startScroll() on close as defensive re-sync of the scrolled-state class.

bugs.error_message: Nav loses .nav-scrolled (background + blur) at the bottom of the page — process/footer text bleeds through a transparent header
bugs.root_cause: The nav used ScrollTrigger.create({ start: 40, end: 'max', toggleClass }). A BOUNDED trigger DEACTIVATES once scroll passes its end, and toggleClass strips the class on deactivation — so at/near the bottom (scroll >= cached max, cache easily stale after the brief/drawer change the page height) the class was removed. Also latent: the effect early-returned under prefers-reduced-motion, so reduced-motion users never got the scrolled nav at all (this is scroll-state styling, not motion).
bugs.fix: Replaced with an unbounded ScrollTrigger.create({ start: 0, end: 'max', onUpdate/onRefresh: (self) => bar.classList.toggle('nav-scrolled', self.scroll() > 40) }) plus an initial apply(window.scrollY) on mount (handles loading mid-scroll via #anchor). Removed the reduced-motion early return so the toggle runs regardless. Reaching/passing the bottom can no longer strip the class.

bugs.error_message: After adding the brief close affordance, the opened brief was invisible/unclickable — real clicks + typing did nothing (chips/inputs never updated); only synthetic el.click() worked
bugs.root_cause: The CTA <div> and the brief-wrap <div> sit at the same position in a {open ? <div> : <div>} conditional, so React RE-USED the same DOM node across the swap. openBrief animates that node to autoAlpha:0 (visibility:hidden) as the CTA; when it became the brief-wrap it kept those inline gsap styles, so the whole brief rendered visibility:hidden (getBoundingClientRect reported a box, but elementFromPoint at that box returned the swap-box ancestor; real pointer/keyboard events can't hit a hidden element, while synthetic el.click() can — which is why the chip state 'worked' via evaluate but not via page.click/type).
bugs.fix: Gave the two conditional <div>s distinct keys (key="brief" / key="cta") so React mounts a fresh node each way, with no carried-over gsap inline styles. Also moved the on-close CTA fade-in + focus into a post-commit useLayoutEffect and switched that fade from autoAlpha to opacity (autoAlpha's visibility:hidden would again block focus() — same trap as bug-004).

bugs.error_message: AmbientField canvas invisible on screen — passes every DOM assertion (present, aria-hidden, pointer-events:none, z<0) but a test rect drawn on it never shows
bugs.root_cause: index.css set background-color on BOTH html and body. When html has its own background, body's background does NOT propagate to the root/page canvas — it paints as an opaque element layer, and in CSS painting order that layer sits ABOVE negative-z-index children. So the z-[-10] fixed ambient canvas was permanently hidden behind body's opaque navy.
bugs.fix: Removed background-color from body; html keeps navy (it propagates to the page canvas so the page is still navy everywhere). Audited body-background dependents — none (the hero rotating-line span uses its own bg-navy class). Canvas stays z-[-10].

bugs.error_message: AmbientField canvas bitmap blank on load (frames=1, 0 painted pixels) — only painted after the first chapter switch
bugs.root_cause: The active chapter's alpha was set statically at init (state[0].alpha = target) and only chapter SWITCHES started a fade; the initial active chapter never got a fade-in that woke the draw loop, and a mid-page hard refresh had no active-chapter paint at all.
bugs.fix: Start all chapter alphas at 0 with activeIdx = -1, then after creating the ScrollTriggers determine the chapter at the viewport centre (getBoundingClientRect) and call setChapter(initial) — a real 0→target fade-in that wakes the loop and paints immediately, correct even when loaded mid-page (e.g. at #contact).

bugs.fix: Added a 2px PAD to every placement boundary in boundsFor() and subtracted 2*PAD from marginMax, so marks always clear each boundary by >=2px — float-robust and visually fully clear.

bugs.error_message: Terminal (02/Code) box height jumps on every log<->matrix phase cycle — distracting
bugs.root_cause: animateToPhase ran a gsap height tween from the current box height to each phase target height every transition, so the box visibly resized each log<->matrix cycle.
bugs.fix: Deleted the height tween. After document.fonts.ready, lockHeight() measures both phases once (log = full build log + metrics offsetHeight; matrix = rows*lineHeight + padding) and pins the body to the taller via style.height. animateToPhase now only flips the data-phase attribute; both phases center content via justify-content:center. Recomputed on resize (rAF-debounced) + ScrollTrigger.refresh().
